title: deploy-canary
description: Constrains the values Helm will accept. It exists because of three measured holes, all of which helm lint and helm template called fine: `--set-string failure.crashLoop=false` rendered a crash-looping pod, because a non-empty string is truthy in a Go template and "false" is a non-empty string; `--set image.pullPolicy=y` rendered a YAML 1.1 boolean that the API server's own deserializer rejects; and `--set image.digest=notadigest` rendered an image reference no registry will resolve. additionalProperties is false everywhere on purpose: `--set failure.crashloop=true`, with the wrong case, silently asked for nothing and installed a healthy pod, which is worse than an error because the caller believes they measured a crash loop.

digest.description: Empty, or a real digest. Empty is the default and means the tag above is what runs.

replicaCount.description: At least one. Zero renders a Deployment that can never fail the way this chart is for.

failure.description: The switches this chart exists for. Booleans, and only booleans, and at most one of them true: the template refuses two because they are not independent.

path.description: The path the HTTP GET asks for. It has to be one the server actually serves: this container serves a directory, so anything other than / is a 404 and a 404 restarts the container.

readiness.description: No path here on purpose. Readiness is an exec that looks for a file, and the difference between the two mechanisms is the subject of this chart.

cpu.description: A Kubernetes quantity. Whole cores may be written as a number, so both types are allowed and the pattern applies to the string form.

memory.description: A Kubernetes quantity. `abc` is accepted by helm and rejected by the API server's decoder, which is a failure that only appears on a cluster.
